body:
Define what a design holds and what makes one valid, so every later Design task builds on one definition. This task saves nothing and adds no page.

### Do

- Record the format in a new decision. A cursory suggestion, not a prescription: JSON, holding a schema version, an ID, a title, the tab it belongs to (`architecture` or `ui`), and a tree of elements.
- An element has a permanent ID, a type and properties, and may have children. A child's position lives on its parent.
- Add a validator on the server. It refuses an unknown schema version or tab, a repeated element ID, an unknown element type, an unknown property, a value outside a property's closed list, and children under a type that can't hold them. A refusal names the element and what is wrong.
- Keep element types and their properties in one table that later tasks extend. Start with only what the tests need; the UI/UX and Architecture tasks add the real ones.
- Solace will support many diagram types (flow, sequence and others), so a new one must not need a format change.

### Constraints

A design is data, not code: no Gleam, Lustre or CSS in the format, and it stays out of the symbol store and type checks.

### Acceptance

- Unit tests: a valid design passes, and each refusal above is refused with the element named.

### Left out

Saving, versions, the page, and the real element types.
title: design: format and validity rules
